CVE-2026-83813.title: Twisted: DNS Response Spoofing in twisted.names Due to Missing Source Address Validation
CVE-2026-83813.description: Twisted is an event-based framework for internet applications, supporting Python 3.6+. An attacker able to deliver a packet to the resolver's listening port with the correct transaction ID can inject a forged answer. CVE-2026-92446.title: GUIX binary resource loader reads past the end of a resource, because no length for it ever reaches the loader
CVE-2026-92446.description:
`gx_binres_theme_load()` and `gx_binres_font_load()` take the resource as a bare `GX_UBYTE *` with no length, and `GX_BINRES_DATA_INFO` has no field to carry one. Every read is therefore performed at an offset the file itself chose, against a buffer whose extent the loader does not know. A resource that declares more data than it contains is read past its end, and an offset stored in the file is turned into a pointer without being bounded.

This is a distinct defect from GHSA-hgcj-22cg-4hfv, which was an underflowed glyph count. It needs no underflow and no wrapped multiply: a perfectly well-formed, narrow glyph range reaches it.

unlink SCO child
drop link's parent reference
clear child->parent
release ACL parent
bt_link_release()
kfree(parent)
hci_dev_unlock()
read parent->features[0][3]

alive after unlinking. Commit 42de40abe25d ("Bluetooth: hci_conn: fix the
SCO setup context lifetime") protects the child…

CVE-2026-98743.title: ASoC: codecs: rt1017-sdca-sdw: fix uninitialized stream_config->type
CVE-2026-98743.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ASoC: codecs: rt1017-sdca-sdw: fix uninitialized stream_config->type

stream_config is not initialized before being passed to
sdw_stream_add_slave(). The type field may contain garbage and is
later copied to stream->type by sdw_config_stream().

Zero-initialize stream_config so type defaults to SDW_STREAM_PCM.

While at it, use snd_sdw_params_to_config() helper instead of
open-coding the same logic.

CVE-2026-99090.title: drm/amdgpu: serialize vblank counter reads against GPU reset
CVE-2026-99090.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

drm/amdgpu: serialize vblank counter reads against GPU reset

The vblank counter callback reads display registers and scanout
position without holding reset_domain->sem. During GPU recovery,
display commit work can call the callback while reset owns the
semaphore for writing. The hardware access then triggers the
lockdep_assert_held() in amdgpu_device_skip_hw_access() and sets
TAINT_WARN when lockdep is enabled.

Try to acquire the reset semaphore for reading before accessing the
hardware, and hold it across the counter and scanout-position reads.
If reset is already in progress, return DRM's cached software vblank
count instead. This avoids blocking behind reset and avoids accessing
display hardware while it is being reset.

used only when reset prevents a safe hardware read. This addresses

CVE-2026-99151.title: drm/amd/display: Fix NULL sink dereference in USB4 bandwidth functions
CVE-2026-99151.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

drm/amd/display: Fix NULL sink dereference in USB4 bandwidth functions

allocate_usb4_bandwidth_for_stream() and allocate_usb4_bandwidth() both
use ASSERT(stream->sink) before dereferencing stream->sink->link. ASSERT
is compiled out in production builds, so a NULL stream->sink causes a
NULL pointer dereference.

link_set_dpms_off() already guards two earlier accesses to stream->sink
with explicit NULL checks, confirming that stream->sink can legitimately
be NULL. The subsequent call to deallocate_usb4_bandwidth() had no
equivalent guard.

Replace the ASSERT() calls with proper NULL checks that return false
early, and add a matching stream->sink guard at the call site in
link_set_dpms_off() consistent with the surrounding pattern.
